newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates sluggish, Suezmax seen better.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates sluggish, Suezmax seen better.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates were little changed on Monday in a sluggish start to the week but shipping brokers said there was some evidence that recent losses may have come to an end.
"Activity fell last week with rates experiencing a slight correction downwards," said a broker. "It's been quiet again today but there are one or two encouraging signs".
The Middle East Gulf market was thin, with many Japanese and Korean December requirements already covered. Indian Suezmax enquiries provided the only active interest, they added.

The Shipping Corp of India (SCI) was looking for two million-barrel vessels loading in the first 10 days of the month after fixing the Winner on Friday to take a 120,000-tonne cargo loading December 2.
Much international activity remained subdued as business got off to a slow start after a two-day U.S. holiday last week, brokers said.
There was no VLCC interest on West African markets either but brokers reported three Suezmax fixings into Europe at W90-W95 for the second decade of the month.
Inter-UK Cont Aframax rates perked up a shade, brokers said.

Spanish refiners fixed two vessels to take 80,000-tonne cargoes from the Flotta terminal in the first half of December at W102.50, five points up on Friday but most brokers pegged the market at about W100 after Elf fixed the Alandia Pride for W95.
In the Mediterranean, brokers reported another slight pick-up in rates for Aframax owners with Repsol fixing the Armata for a cross-Med voyage at W112.50.
Suezmax fixings were few and far between with activity limited to the London Pride, taken by Elf for a voyage from Sidi Kreir loading on December 9.
